variants.name: Orbital Silk
variants.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Asset: refined minimal luminous background image for a dark blue/lilac Art-Net LED controller web interface.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET Orbital Traces. Images 2, 3, 4 are SUPPORTING STYLE references for violet angular circuitry, cyan glossy twin traces, and iridescent parallel etched traces.
Preserve the recognizable LED dotted panel arrangement, relative locations, silhouettes and original dot colors from image 1. Keep dots individually separated and crisp.
Change composition to a wider landscape 16:9 canvas, extend the space horizontally around the central LED architecture. Circuit traces should reach across the entire canvas including corners, top and bottom, becoming faint and smoothly fading out rather than abruptly ending. Retain only the gracefully CURVED ORBITAL ARCS ON THE LEFT of the LED architecture. REMOVE ALL LARGE CURVES/ARCS ON THE RIGHT: right half must contain angular straight PCB traces only. Do not wrap arcs around the scene. Keep left arcs localized entirely in the left third, two or three elegant incomplete sweeps.
Merge fine angular PCB-like line structures of all three supporting refs, including single violet lines, paired cyan hairlines and occasional triples with tiny circular terminals. Distribute these sparingly but broadly through the empty space across the full background.
Add a second depth layer of almost invisible very dark blue/lilac angular traces behind the LED dots, spanning approximately 40–50 percent of the LED panel regions, with the dots clearly in front. A minority of isolated actual LED pixels within the panels should have bright white-cyan or lavender cores and compact soft glow, giving a captured sparkle. Add subtle thin glossy specular shimmer on selected short sections of circuit lines. Most dots and lines remain dim and refined. Avoid large starbursts, broad fog or loud blooming.
Palette: retain original dot colors on almost-black midnight navy, blue, lilac and cyan circuitry; restrained pink iridescence. Elegant minimal abstract etched electronics, visually quiet enough for UI cards layered over it. No text, no UI, no icons, no watermarks, no literal circuit board or chips, no checkerboard, no solid panels behind dots. Deliver ONE full-frame background, not a collage.
Variant direction: Balanced version: particularly delicate silk-thin single and twin lines, layered left orbital arcs, softly distributed horizontal and diagonal circuit branches. Very restrained glints, elegant spacious finish.
variants.refinement_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this background with only these final corrections; preserve the wide canvas, dot-panel silhouettes, all colors, dark balance and angular circuit design exactly. Remove any tiny curved orbital remnants ABOVE the top green/yellow dot panel and to the RIGHT of the main blue/cyan dot panels; replace them with extremely faint straight angular traces. The two large curved arcs on the LEFT stay unchanged. Add scattered compact sparkling LED pixels INSIDE the dotted panels themselves: about 18 individual existing dots across the full stack should have tiny bright white-cyan/lavender cores and soft restrained local glow. This is sparse pinpoint shimmer, not large starbursts. The glow must belong to individual LED dots and not only circuit terminals. Preserve all other dots as dim separate pinpoints. Leave the almost invisible underlay circuits and glossy angular circuit lines across the rest of the full background. No new objects or text.
